exact_statement: For the distinct-Finset version of Erdos 786, let H_N be the hypergraph on {2,...,N} whose edges are supports of disjoint finite subsets S,T with equal products and unequal cardinalities. Prove tau(H_N)=o(N), preferably by converting the audited fractional cover w_N(n)=log(N/n)/log N into an integral transversal; and investigate whether one coherent rule yields an infinite admissible set of natural density greater than 1-epsilon for every epsilon>0. An all-parameter theorem exposing a sharp obstruction to a frozen rounding mechanism may count only as a standalone decisive lemma, not as closure of either density-one assertion.
scope_notes: Variant lock: products are over Finsets, so each integer occurs at most once on either shore. Overlap between shores must be cancelled; coefficients after cancellation lie in {-1,0,1}. Repetitions-allowed additive-function arguments are excluded.
The finite target is exact: H_N has vertex set {2,...,N}; tau(H_N)=o(N) is equivalent to a distinct-factor admissible subset of [N] of size N-o(N), after deleting 1.

The promoted predecessor theorem is a read-only dependency: w_N(n)=log(N/n)/log N is a fractional cover of every bad support and has total weight (1+o(1))N/log N. It supplies feasibility, not integral rounding.

A rounding theorem must exploit arithmetic circuit structure. A generic approximation depending on log|E(H_N)|, maximum edge size, or a fixed cutoff is non-success unless its proved total loss is o(log N).
An all-parameter obstruction must refute a precisely frozen rounding/ownership/coarea mechanism or prove a sharp integrality-gap family. Isolated examples or finite experiments do not count.

The infinite part requires one set with an actual natural-density limit greater than 1-epsilon. Upper/logarithmic density, density along a subsequence, or unrelated finite optimizers are insufficient.
One coherent selection/deletion rule may address both parts, but proving tau(H_N)=o(N) alone settles only the finite distinct-Finset subproblem.
The predecessor campaign erdos-786-distinct-factor-admission-20260824 is immutable and may be cited only through its promoted proof and independent audit.
Public search for a solution to Erdos 786 is prohibited. Ordinary named background theorems may be used with exact hypotheses.

variant_lock.allowed: finite subsets / Finsets of distinct positive integers on each shore
variant_lock.forbidden: multisets, repetition on a shore, or arbitrary integer coefficients
variant_lock.exceptional_elements: delete 1; 0 is excluded from positive-density admissible sets

read_only_dependency.theorem: For every N>=2, w_N(n)=log(N/n)/log N is a fractional transversal of H_N of exact total (N log N-log(N!))/log N-1=(1+o(1))N/log N.

exact_subproblems.finite: Prove tau(H_N)=o(N) for the full unbounded-length bad-relation hypergraph.
exact_subproblems.rounding: Give a uniform arithmetic rounding/ownership rule whose integral cost is o(N), or an all-parameter theorem refuting one precisely frozen such rule.
exact_subproblems.infinite: For every epsilon>0 construct one distinct-Finset admissible A subset N with natural density greater than 1-epsilon; this needs coherence beyond independently optimized finite transversals.
